title: Who Gets the Desk? A Simulated Case Study of Unequal Access in Two School Districts
instructions: 这是一份为B2–C1学习者设计的限时阅读练习，主题是教育系统如何应对入学机会不平等。请先通读文章（约800–1100词），再完成10道题（判断题、填空题、单选题）。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。注意：文章和题目均为模拟材料，不是真实报道，也不代表任何官方考试。建议限时18分钟完成阅读和答题。
passage:
A. In the fictional coastal city of Marlow Bay, two school districts—Northbank and Southfield—serve families with very different resources. Northbank, in the wealthier hills, has three well-equipped primary schools. Southfield, near the industrial port, has one overcrowded primary school and a waiting list of 240 children. Last September, the city council published a report showing that Southfield’s classrooms held an average of 38 pupils, while Northbank’s held 22. The report also noted that Southfield had no library room and only one computer for every 15 students. Northbank had a library in each school and one computer for every 4 students. These numbers are simulated for this case study, but they reflect patterns found in many real cities where wealth and school quality are closely linked.

B. The council did not ignore the gap. In October, it announced a “Fair Start” plan. The plan had three parts. First, the city would build two new classrooms at Southfield Primary by the following September. Second, it would provide 120 used laptops to Southfield, donated by local companies. Third, it would offer free after-school tutoring in reading and maths for children in Southfield, taught by volunteer teachers from Northbank. The council promised that the plan would reduce the average class size in Southfield to 30 within two years. It did not promise to make the two districts equal. “We cannot fix everything at once,” said Councilor Maya Chen. “But we can make the first step fair.” This modest aim was deliberate: the council wanted to show progress without raising expectations it could not meet.

C. Not everyone was satisfied. Parent groups in Southfield argued that the plan was too slow. “Two new classrooms will not help my son this year,” said Fatima Osman, a mother of two. “And 120 laptops for 900 children is not enough.” Some Northbank parents worried about the tutoring scheme. “Our teachers are already busy,” said one parent, who asked not to be named. “If they spend time in Southfield, who will teach our children?” The council replied that tutoring would be voluntary and would happen after school hours, so Northbank pupils would not lose lessons. The council also said that Northbank teachers would receive extra pay for the tutoring, a detail intended to answer concerns about workload and fairness.

D. A second problem was transport. Southfield families live up to 5 kilometres from the school, and the city bus runs only twice a day. The Fair Start plan did not include a school bus. When asked why, the council said that a bus was “too expensive for now” and that the city would “look at it again next year.” Parent representatives pointed out that children who miss the bus often miss school. The council’s own data showed that Southfield’s attendance rate was 87%, compared with 96% in Northbank. The report did not say that transport was the only cause of absence, but it listed transport as a “major barrier.” This gap in the plan showed how budgets can shape which problems are addressed first.

E. In January, a local charity offered to fund a minibus for one year. The council accepted the offer, but with a condition: the minibus would run only on weekdays and only for children in years 1 to 6. Older pupils would still need to find their own way. “It is better than nothing,” said Fatima Osman, “but my daughter is in year 8. She still walks.” The charity said it could not afford a larger bus. The council said it would review the situation in December, leaving older students and their families in an uncertain position for most of the year.

F. By March, some changes were visible. The first new classroom was open, and the average class size in Southfield had fallen from 38 to 34. The laptops had arrived, but only 80 were working; 40 needed repairs. The tutoring programme had started with 15 volunteer teachers, not the 30 the council had hoped for. Attendance in Southfield had risen slightly, to 89%. Northbank’s attendance remained at 96%. Councilor Chen called the results “a good beginning, not a victory.” She added that the city would publish a full report in June, which would give a clearer picture of what had worked and what had not.

G. Critics noted that the plan measured success in averages, not in individual children. “An average class size of 34 still means some classes have 40 children,” said one education researcher, who was not involved in the plan. “And a laptop that does not work is not a laptop.” The council agreed that repairs were slow but said that a local repair shop had offered to fix the remaining machines for free. The researcher also asked whether the tutoring would continue after the first year. The council said it would depend on funding. No decision had been made by March, so the programme’s future remained unclear.

H. The case of Marlow Bay shows that responding to unequal access is not a single decision but a series of small, imperfect steps. The city did not promise equality. It promised a smaller gap. Some steps helped quickly; others were delayed. Parents in Southfield welcomed the new classroom but still asked for a bus for all children. Parents in Northbank welcomed the extra pay for teachers but still worried about time. The council promised more reports. Whether the gap will close remains an open question—one that the June report may begin to answer.

grammar.title: 否定、比较、数量范围和时态：限定词的含义
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，否定词（not, no, never）、比较结构（more than, less than, as...as）、数量限定词（some, any, enough, only, all, both）以及时态（过去、现在、将来）共同决定句子的准确含义。例如：'not enough' 表示数量不足；'only' 强调限制；'did not promise' 表示过去没有承诺；'will reduce' 表示将来会减少。理解这些词可以帮助我们判断一句话是肯定还是否定、是全部还是部分、是过去还是将来。
grammar.example: The council promised that the plan would reduce the average class size in Southfield to 30 within two years. It did not promise to make the two districts equal.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence: The city ______ build a new school last year.
questions.explanation: last year 表示过去时间，否定过去动作要用 did not + 动词原形。
questions.evidence: The city did not build a new school last year.

questions.prompt: There are ______ laptops for all the students. Many students still have no computer.
questions.explanation: 后句说许多学生仍没有电脑，说明笔记本电脑数量不足，因此用 not enough。
questions.evidence: There are not enough laptops for all the students.

questions.explanation: 比较两个地区电脑数量，用比较级 more...than。
questions.evidence: Northbank has more computers than Southfield.

questions.prompt: The council ______ publish the full report next June.
questions.explanation: next June 表示将来，用 will + 动词原形。
questions.evidence: The council will publish the full report next June.

questions.prompt: ______ the parents were happy with the plan. Some were, but some were not.
questions.explanation: 后句说有些家长满意，有些不满意，说明不是全部满意，用 Not all。
questions.evidence: Not all the parents were happy with the plan.

questions.explanation: 表示“仅仅在工作日运行”，用 only 强调限制。
questions.evidence: The minibus runs only on weekdays.

questions.prompt: Southfield’s attendance rate is ______ than Northbank’s.
questions.explanation: 比较两个出勤率，用比较级 lower...than。
questions.evidence: Southfield’s attendance rate is lower than Northbank’s.

questions.prompt: The council ______ promised to make the districts equal.
questions.explanation: 原文说“It did not promise to make the two districts equal.” 这里描述过去没有承诺，用 did not。
questions.evidence: The council did not promise to make the districts equal.
